analysis.title: CoreWe've Got Bills To Pay: Bernstein Sees $76 Billion Funding Hole At Imploding Neocloud
key_insights: Bernstein (Madison Rezaei, Underperform since initiation seven months ago) cut its CRWV price target to $51 from $74 and its target EV/EBIT multiple to 23.5x from 25.5x, citing cost of capital as CoreWeave moves to shorter-dated contracts.

Bernstein estimates CRWV needs to raise $85B to fund its existing committed backlog, $9B of which is covered by existing facilities. That leaves about $76B of new money before any new contract is signed.
Goldman's follow-up note (Gabriela Borges, Buy upgrade on Monday) puts the funding gap at about $23B. Bernstein's figure is more than three times larger.

Bernstein says stopping new contract wins would not fix the funding need. Deployment obligations in existing contracts plus maintenance and replacement capex still have to be paid, so profitability would not improve immediately.

Bernstein models about $46B of growth capex next year plus about $6B of maintenance capex, for $52.5B in 2027, above consensus. Even with no future backlog, 2027 capex is $43.5B. Its capex is well below the Street from 2028 on.
Bernstein widens its 2026 and 2027 adjusted EPS losses and models adjusted losses through at least 2029.

Goldman's $23B depends on assumptions. It assumes 80% DDTL debt financing, nets $10.6B of undrawn DDTL capacity and $10.4B of cash optionality, and assumes customers prepay 20% of contract value ($15.7B). Stretching GPU useful life to six years lowers it to $19.5B.

The article challenges Goldman's inputs. CoreWeave's prepayment percentages have fallen over six months, and the $10.4B of cash optionality includes $2.2B of ATM share sales at $64 (above the current price). It also counts a revolver of which $1.2B of $2.5B is already drawn per Bernstein.

Goldman's 4.2GW scenario ($38B) assumes $52.7B of customer prepayments. Without them, new debt needed is $84.5B at a 94% debt-to-loan ratio, above the 80% DDTL cap Goldman cites. Goldman's note gives no cost of capital and defers to a 10% new-debt cost in its upgrade note.

Goldman's own model shows free cash burn of $28.2B in 2026, $28.2B in 2027 and $15.8B in 2028, with debt rising $26.7B, $26.6B and $20.0B. Long-term debt rises from $14.9B (end 2025) to $90.8B (2028), interest coverage is 0.3x in 2026 and 0.7x in 2027, and cash falls to $1.2B at end 2027.
Goldman discloses it is a manager or co-manager of a pending CoreWeave underwriting, owns 1% or more of the stock, and expects to seek investment banking compensation within three months.

CoreWeave has $42.1B of debt and a $3.3B annual interest bill, a blended 7.8% rate held down by $10.8B of 2-3% converts. Gross debt is 8.6x LTM adjusted EBITDA, 11.7x on total committed capacity and 7.4x next year's EBITDA.

Most debt matures in 2030-2032 (about $31B), so Bernstein does not expect distress soon. DDTLs amortize, with principal repayments and covenant tests starting well before maturity: DDTL 5.0 repayments begin around Oct 22 (CoreWeave says November), the first 1.35x DSCR test is around Nov 30, DDTL 5.5 amortizes from January and the $8.5B DDTL 4.0 next July.
Unsecured bonds yield around 15%. DDTL 5.5 (August) priced at SOFR+5.50%, the widest since the first DDTL in 2023, and Bernstein thinks later deals could price higher.

Shorter enterprise contracts capture higher pricing per MW but are riskier to creditors and do not lower CoreWeave's cost of capital. Bernstein assigns a low, nonzero probability to CoreWeave building a differentiated enterprise business.

Bernstein's best-case Meta contract (including the $21B expansion) gives an unlevered IRR of 9-12% (9% illustrative). The levered IRR is 32%, driven by leverage and a $2.3B residual value in year six. HSBC reached a similar conclusion with an 8.9% ROIC.

Bernstein does not call CRWV a zero because of its large backlog, line of sight to powered shell delivery and contracts that are not underwater. It thinks Nvidia would intervene in a true downside, which raises the floor but does not necessarily re-energize the stock.

Bernstein calls the damage semi-contained: if CoreWeave ceased to exist, colo contracts would be absorbed. The article argues CoreWeave is still the AI credit beta barometer and the tenant on seven of the 20 project-finance data center bonds in the junk market.

Price action: after Goldman's Monday upgrade the stock spiked to $66 premarket and gave back the gain after the open. HSBC set a $39 target on Tuesday. The stock fell another 8% to $56.70, below its pre-upgrade level and the 52-week low.

market_movers.rationale: Bernstein cut its target from $74 on a $76B funding need, 15% unsecured funding costs and about 9% unlevered returns on its best contract.
Goldman upgraded to Buy on Monday while cutting its price target by almost a quarter. Its follow-up note sizes the funding gap at about $23B.
HSBC set a $39 target, arguing the more CoreWeave invests, the more value is destroyed. It cites an 8.9% ROIC.

sector_views.rationale: Bernstein says damage is semi-contained, but the article notes neocloud listings keep falling and CoreWeave anchors junk-market data center bonds.

earnings_insights: Bernstein widens its 2026 and 2027 adjusted EPS loss estimates (forecast, not reported), with adjusted losses through at least 2029. The source text garbles the figures: 4.56 and 4.77 appear alongside 5.14 and 6.81, so which pairs are new versus prior is unclear.
Bernstein 2027 capex estimate (forecast): about $46B growth plus about $6B maintenance, total $52.5B, above consensus. In a no-additional-backlog case it is $43.5B.
Goldman model estimates (forecast): free cash flow of -$28.2B in 2026, -$28.2B in 2027 and -$15.8B in 2028 on capex of $38.6B, $48.0B and $49.9B. Interest expense is about $6B a year.

Bernstein reports CoreWeave debt of $42.1B as of Oct 20 with a $3.3B annual interest bill. Management says contracts signed since 2Q have materially better economics, which Bernstein says may be too small to change blended returns.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Widest spread since the first DDTL in 2023. Bernstein uses it as the best proxy for new secured funding cost and expects later deals could price higher.

risk_factors: Funding need of about $76B (Bernstein) to deliver the existing backlog, with unsecured credit available at 15%+ rates.
Amortizing DDTLs bring principal repayments and covenant tests (first 1.35x DSCR test around Nov 30) before final maturity.
Customer prepayments are falling, so Goldman's lower funding estimate may not hold.
Shorter enterprise contracts are riskier to creditors and do not lower the cost of capital.
Returns are thin: 9% unlevered on the best contract against new money costing 9% secured and 15% unsecured.
Levered returns depend on the residual value of six-year-old GPUs.
Goldman's own model shows interest coverage of 0.3x in 2026, 0.7x in 2027, and net debt to equity peaking at 3,059% in 2027.
Contagion risk to AI credit, including seven of 20 junk-market project-finance data center bonds with CoreWeave as tenant.
Bernstein's upside risks: the stock is volatile and momentum-driven, and Nvidia may intervene in a true downside.

tension_points.bull_case: Goldman (Buy) sizes the gap at about $23B. Customers prepay about 20% of contract value, 80% of capex is DDTL-financed and GPU useful life stretches to six years.
tension_points.bear_case: Bernstein (Underperform) puts it at $76B funded at 15%+ unsecured rates. Prepayment percentages have fallen, and Goldman's own model shows $46.6B of new debt in two years plus about $50B of lease liabilities.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The first 1.35x DSCR covenant test on DDTL 5.0 around November 30, and DDTL 5.0 monthly repayments beginning around Oct 22 (CoreWeave says November).

tension_points.bull_case: Bernstein says CRWV is not a zero given its large backlog and powered shell delivery, and thinks Nvidia would intervene in a true downside, which raises the floor.
tension_points.bear_case: Intervention does not necessarily re-energize the stock. The business earns about 9% unlevered against new money costing 9% secured and 15% unsecured, and medium-term economics likely resemble the older contracts.

theme_stances.key_argument: CoreWeave needs about $76B of new money just to deliver its existing backlog, at funding costs near 15% for a business earning about 9% unlevered.
Bernstein sees damage as semi-contained, with colo contracts absorbed if CoreWeave ceased to exist.
